# Introduction

Reproducible reports should connect assumptions, analysis, evidence, and interpretation without forcing readers to reconstruct the workflow. This template uses Quarto for authoring and computation, Typst for the formal PDF, and an optional HTML output for interactive reading. Its modular structure is intended for research collaborations in which different contributors own different sections.

The worked example studies a damped oscillator. It is deliberately small, but it illustrates the same mechanisms used in larger research reports: mathematical definitions, executable analysis, cross-referenced figures and tables, and bibliographic citations. The visualisation follows the principle that graphics should make structure in data easier to inspect [@wickham2016].

::: {.callout-note title="How to use this template"}
Edit the metadata at the top of `report.qmd`, keep the Introduction, Conclusions, Acknowledgements, and references in this main file, and place project-specific middle sections in underscore-prefixed files under `sections/`.
:::

# Conclusions

The template provides a single source for a formal Typst PDF and a navigable HTML companion. Mathematical expressions, citations, callouts, tables, and computational results remain consistent across both formats. Python source is hidden by default, while selected cells can explicitly override that behavior when a collaborator needs to inspect the implementation.
